suite.description: Control Resource profile vectors (SERVICE-CONTROL-PROFILE-01 §12): the initial change, admission SC0 to SC7 for every cell of the mutation table of §3 and every writer class of §2.3, state validation of written entries, and replica transitions (a superseded question concurrent with an answer, two concurrent answers, two base approvals, revocation, an unknown op, deletion of a request).

conventions.changes: Every change is made with time 0 and no message by the SHARED-OBJECTS-PROFILE-01 §8 actor of its writer in C (fixtures.resources.C); each change is carried by its writer's Data Unit whose actor sequence equals the change's Automerge sequence. A validation case gives the change and its causal history (context.history, in delivery order).
conventions.control: inputs.control_ref names a fixtures.control_states entry: C's Control state at the Data Unit's control_ref. inputs.writer_class is the class of §2.3 derived from it and, for a kind-1 device, from the approvals of the change's pre-state; an implementation derives it itself.
conventions.principals: Principal keys are h('LFCP-TV-SC-' + label + '-ED25519') and h('LFCP-TV-SC-' + label + '-X25519') as Ed25519 and X25519 seeds; Resource IDs are h('LFCP-TV-SC-RESOURCE-' + name). Only descriptors and IDs are published.
conventions.diagnostics: A refused change is PROFILE_INVALID with the first diagnostic in the order of §4; an admitted change is valid.
conventions.links: args.link of a pair-section request is an opaque test string, not a pairing link of IDENTITY-PROFILE-01 §5.2.

suite.warning: All keys in this suite are public test fixtures. They MUST NOT be used in production.

cases.description: question_superseded and answer_created, each made on question_created, delivered in both orders, then the service's rejection

rule.text: The service's superseded and a human's answer are made concurrently and both admitted; the service then rejects the answer with snapshot_changed and can no longer resolve the question.

assertions: Both delivery orders give the same document.
question_resolved_after_superseded (refused) shows that a superseded question is never resolved: resolved and superseded are exclusive.

cases.description: answer_created (A) and answer_concurrent (R), each made on question_created, delivered in both orders, then question_resolved

rule.text: Two answers to one question are made concurrently and both admitted; the service accepts the first it executes and rejects the other with already_answered.

assertions: Both delivery orders give the same document.

cases.description: A second base approval, B2's refused heartbeat, the revocation of B2's approval and B's admitted heartbeat

rule.text: Two valid base approvals without revoked give the class service to nobody; after root or personal revokes one, the other device's changes are admitted again.

assertions: The refused change is not merged and blocks its dependants (SOP §14.1).

cases.description: The unknown op export-logs and its rejection

rule.text: An unknown op is admitted; a version-1 service answers rejected{unsupported_op} and writes nothing else.

assertions: unknown_op_rejected changes only events[r2]: the request has no effect.
The client shows the update text of §11 for the code unsupported_op.

cases.description: revoke_base_b, B's concurrent status write and B's write made on the revocation, in both orders

rule.text: The class is taken on the causal history: a change made before the revocation stays admitted wherever it is delivered; one made on the revocation is refused.

assertions: A replica never re-judges an admitted change at its current head.

cases.description: The life of r1: created, received, executing, applied, deleted with its event

rule.text: A request is deleted only by the service and only once its event is final; the rid is never reused.

assertions: request_deleted_without_event and request_deleted_before_final (refused) show the deletion before the final event.
request_recreated_after_deletion (refused) shows that the rid is never reused (§10).
